This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Seven Creeks downstream of Euroa including Kialla West. Information is also included for the other waterways in the area. 

Moderate level flooding is happening along the Seven Creeks at Kialla West 
Minor level Goulburn River flooding is possible at Shepparton from early Wednesday morning.
Moderate level Broken River flooding is occurring at Orrvale.

Rainfall across the Seven and Castle Creeks catchments since Sunday morning has resulted in creek level rises and minor to moderate flooding. 

Seven Creeks downstream of Euroa - Correction at 6pm
The Seven Creeks at Kialla West is currently at 5.32 with moderate flooding, and may peak near 5.70 metres overnight Tuesday into Wednesday. 

As of Tuesday Morning, the Midland Highway to Benalla is closed between Nalinga and Goorambat due to deep floodwater over the road, with detours in place. 
Prepare for flooding now. Take actions to protect your life and property against potential hazards caused by flooding.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater. 
  • Follow your emergency plan and locate your emergency kit, if you have one. 
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground. 
  • If you are camping close to a creek or river, you may be at risk of flooding and need to move to higher ground, away from waterways.
To check if your property is prone to flooding:
Check the Goulburn Broken Catchment Management Authority's Community Flood Information Portal and download your property information statement at: https://my.floodreport.com.au/gbcma/

For full instructions, and more local flood information, download the Shepparton, Mooropna & Kialla Local Flood Guide at: www.ses.vic.gov.au/plan-and-stay-safe/flood-guides/greater-shepparton-city-council
Impacts in your area:

  • Low-lying Camping areas along the creek may be flooded
  • Raftery Road, Kialla is likely to flood between the bridge and Edgewater Road, with Arcadia Downs traffic detoured.

properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge at Bandiana.

Moderate flooding easing at Bandiana
Minor flooding occurring at Kiewa (Mainstream)
  • Moderate to heavy rainfall associated with a strong cold front has caused river level rises and Minor to Moderate flooding across the Kiewa River catchment.
Kiewa River downstream of Mongans Bridge
  • Moderate flooding is easing at Bandiana and Minor flooding is occurring at Kiewa Mainstream.
  • The Kiewa River at Bandiana is currently at 3.11 metres and steady, with Moderate flooding. The Kiewa River at Bandiana may fall below the Moderate flood level (3.10 metres) Tuesday afternoon. 
  • The river is likely to remain above the Minor flood level (2.80 metres) at Bandiana for the next few days.
Kiewa River to Mongans Bridge
  • Minor flooding has eased at Mongans Bridge.
The Kiewa River Channel at Kiewa
  • Is currently at 3.39 metres and steady, with Minor flooding. 
  • The Kiewa River Channel at Kiewa is likely to remain above the minor flood level (3.30 metres) during Tuesday and into Wednesday.

Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. 
Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • Rising floodwater can be dangerous. Be aware of water levels rising near you.
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground if still safe to do.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.

Impacts in your area:

At about a river height of 3.1 metres, a Moderate Level Flood at Bandiana
  • Farmland may flood in low sections of the Kiewa River floodplain. 
  • The Cudgewa to Wodonga Rail Trail near the Kiewa Valley Highway is likely to be flooded.
At about a river height of 3.2 metres at Bandiana
  • Conisbee Lane off the Murray Valley Highway floods, isolating one property. 
  • Other properties at risk of being isolated in: Gullifer Lane, Smith Road, Pollards Road and McIntosh Road.
ROAD CLOSURES in the Bandiana area
  • Whytes Road, Baranduda - Road closed at Middle Creek due to flooding. Avoid the area and seek an alternate route. 
  • Check the Vic Traffic website traffic.transport.vic.gov.au for road closures in the area and follow instructions from emergency services.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Broken River downstream of Casey Weir to Orrvale and Kialla. 

Moderate Flooding Possible at Orrvale Wednesday Morning
Moderate flooding is occuring now on the Seven Creeks at Kialla West. 
Minor flooding is possible along the Goulburn River at Shepparton early Wednesday morning. 
Minor flooding at Benalla is easing. 

Rainfall across the Broken River catchment since Sunday has caused river level rises with minor to moderate flooding. No further significant rainfall is forecast for the catchment this week. 

The Broken River at Orrvale is currently at 5.64 metres and is likely to exceed the minor flood level (6.80 metres) overnight Tuesday into Wednesday. 

The river may reach the moderate flood level (7.20 metres) at Orrvale Wednesday morning, but further rises are still possible as upstream flows arrive overnight.
Prepare for flooding now. Take actions to protect your life and property against potential hazards caused by flooding. 
What you should do:
  • People in Orrvale, Kialla Lakes and surrounding riverside areas should follow their emergency plan and locate their emergency kit, if they have one. 
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground. 
  • Floodwater is dangerous and toxic - never drive, walk, play or swim in floodwater.
  • If your property is prone to flooding, check the Goulburn Broken Catchment Management Authority's Community Flood Information Portal and download your property information statement at: https://my.floodreport.com.au/gbcma/
  • For full instructions, and more local flood information, download the Shepparton, Mooropna & Kialla Local Flood Guide at: https://www.ses.vic.gov.au/plan-and-stay-safe/flood-guides/greater-shepparton-city-council
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:
  • Floodwater will cover some farmland and a small number of properties around Doyles Road. 
  • Floodwater may cover parts of Kialla Lakes Drive and Gordon Drive, with many local streets in Kialla Lakes likely to have water over the road as the river rises. 
  • All vehicle & walking tracks within the Arcadia Streamside Reserve, Shepparton Regional Park & Gemmills Swamp Wildlife Reserve are closed, except for Park Bend off Rudd Road. 
If the Broken River at Orrvale rises higher than 7.20 metres overnight, further impacts may occur. A new warning will be issued this evening. 
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 12/08/2026 04:00 pm or as the situation changes.

RIVER LEVELS CLOSE TO THE MAJOR FLOOD LEVEL AND AROUND A PEAK AT WANGARATTA

Impacts in your area:

  • This flood is expected to peak close to 12.70 metres, this is about 12 cm higher than the June 2026 flood peak of 12.58 metres. 
  • Floodwater may reach between Yogi's nose and eyes in APEX park. Floodwater from the King River may fill the Kaluna Wetlands into Merriwa Park. 
  • Bickerton Street and Mundgee Place carparks are flooded, and Painters Island Caravan Park is now closed.

  • Floodwater will enter backyards and low-lying garages and sheds along Templeton Street and Baker Street. 
  • Many river and creek walking paths and bike tracks are now closed. There will be extensive local road closures - drive with care and never enter floodwater. 
  • Floodplains and farmland to the North, South and East of Wangaratta have started to flood, including around the airport, Tarrawingee, Markwood, Oxley Flats, Londrigan, Bowser, Docker Plains and North Wangaratta areas. 
  • Check the Wangaratta Local Flood Guide for more local impacts and advice https://www.ses.vic.gov.au/plan-and-stay-safe/flood-guides/rural-city-of-wangaratta#wangaratta-local-flood-guide
Road Closures
  • The Great Alpine Road is closed at Yellow Creek. A detour is in place via Detour Road.
  • Many local roads may be flooded. For the latest road closures go to:  www.traffic.transport.vic.gov.au and obey ROAD CLOSED signs and follow instructions from emergency services.

Impacts in your area - Whorouly: Widespread farmland with Minor level flooding. 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to the river.
  • The Snow Road may be flooded between the Great Alpine Road and Carboor-Everton Road.

This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for Goulburn River Seymour to Shepparton including Mooroopna.
Information is also included for the other waterways in the area.

Minor level Goulburn River flooding is possible at Shepparton from early Wednesday morning.
Moderate level Seven Creeks flooding is occurring at Kialla West.
Moderate level Broken River flooding is occurring at Orrvale.

  • Moderate to heavy rainfall has caused river level rises across the Goulburn River catchment since Sunday. 
  • Minor flooding is occurring at Seymour and may extend downstream to Shepparton from early Wednesday morning, as the flood peak arrives.
  • The situation is being closely monitored, and this warning will be updated as required.
Goulburn River Seymour to Shepparton
  • The Goulburn River at Shepparton is currently at 7.27 metres and rising, below the minor flood level. 
  • The Goulburn River at Shepparton may exceed the Minor flood level (9.50 metres) early Wednesday morning. 
  • Further rises are possible as upstream flows arrive.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION for the Shepparton-Mooroopna area
In Mooroopna
  • Impacts from Goulburn River flooding are not expected unless the Goulburn River at Shepparton gauge reaches 10.03 metres.
The Broken River at Orrvale 
  • The Broken River may reach the Moderate flood level 7.20 metres at Orrvale Wednesday morning, but further rises are still possible as upstream flows arrive overnight.   
The Seven Creeks at Kialla
  • Moderate flooding above 5.0 metres is occurring now on the Seven Creeks at Kialla West.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.

  • Check the Goulburn Broken Catchment Management Authority's Community Flood Information Portal and download your property information statement at: https://my.floodreport.com.au/gbcma/

Impacts in your area: 
  • Low-lying camping areas along the river will be flooded.
  • High river levels and potential flooding of farmland and parks close to the rivers and creeks.
No two floods are ever the same. In this flood, the Shepparton area is special.
Floodwater is coming from three directions and waterways: the Goulburn River , the Broken River and the Seven Creeks.
This can make predicting what will actually happen more difficult than other floods.

In the Shepparton and Mooroopna area, 
  • The Ross Edwards Causeway is not expected to close.
  • When the Goulburn River reaches the Minor flood level of 9.5 metres: Watt Road and Raftery Road start to flood.
  • In Mooroopna, impacts from Goulburn River flooding are not expected unless the Goulburn River at Shepparton gauge reaches 10.03 metres.
